title: Orsen and the Letter
premise: In the winter of 1918, Isandro Galloway drives for Edith Marlowe, a suffragist whose letters to a network of allies carry more than pleasantries — they carry evidence of a local magistrate's wartime profiteering. When the river bridge closes for the season, Isandro, who has quietly read every letter, is trapped inside the town with the secret and the man who wants it buried. As the armistice approaches, Isandro must choose between the invisibility they have always trusted and putting their own name on the record, ending with the truth published hours before the guns fall silent — and the magistrate's fall, bought at the cost of Isandro's old life.
about_author: Lena Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from the Great War's home front. She writes from a farmhouse in the river country, where she keeps a drawer of unsent letters of her own.

chapters.title: The Man Who Reads First
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Establishes the routine: letters sealed, steamed open, memorized, resealed, delivered. Isandro insists they are only a witness to other people's history. Emotional beat: the comfort and quiet shame of invisible knowledge.

chapters.title: Madam Marlowe's Correspondence
chapters.summary: Edith Marlowe's POV. We see her side: the suffrage network, her coded phrasing, her trust in a driver she believes cannot read. Isandro delivers a letter to Magistrate Corven himself. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Early ice closes the bridge; the ferry is suspended. The town seals itself for the season. Corven's clerk watches Isandro too closely at the post office. Emotional beat: the trap springing shut, disguised as weather.

chapters.title: What the Letters Say
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, flashback-laced. Isandro pieces together Corven's scheme: requisitioned grain sold back at famine prices, soldiers' pensions skimmed. The realization that history has been happening here all along. Emotional beat: vertigo of complicity.

chapters.title: A Driver's Place
chapters.summary: Corven's POV. He notices the driver's steady eyes and begins probing Isandro's background — an orphan, no surname of record, no one to vouch. Emotional beat: menace delivered as courtesy.

chapters.title: The Unsent Drawer
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith reveals, obliquely, that she once lost a sister to Corven's court and has spent years building the case in letters. She tests Isandro with a deliberately false detail. Emotional beat: two watchers recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Ice on the River
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A boy nearly drowns retrieving a dropped letter; Isandro saves him and the letter both, and the town begins to see the driver. Emotional beat: invisibility cracking from the outside in.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, night infiltration. Isandro copies pages from Corven's requisition ledger into memory and a hidden notebook. Nearly caught by the clerk. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Armistice Rumors
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. News that peace may come within weeks; once it does, victors' historians will write the record and Corven's friends will burn the files. The deadline crystallizes. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening into strategy.

chapters.title: A Name of One's Own
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro confronts their own lack of identity — no birth record, no vote, no legal existence — and understands Corven's power rests on exactly this erasure. Emotional beat: the personal fusing with the political.

chapters.title: The Confession Letter
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith drafts the full account for the network, and asks Isandro, plainly, whether they can read. The lie of years stands between them. Emotional beat: betrayal offered a chance to become alliance.

chapters.title: Steam and Truth
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro confesses everything: every letter read, every secret kept. Edith's fury, then a colder calculation — the one person Corven underestimates is the one who knows everything. Emotional beat: rupture becoming partnership.

chapters.title: The Clerk Defects
chapters.summary: Clerk Hobb's POV. Hobb, sickened by the pension skimming that starved his own mother, brings a missing page. Corven suspects and sets a watch on the Marlowe house. Emotional beat: fear choosing a side.

chapters.title: Search of the House
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Corven's men ransack Marlowe House; the confession letter is nearly found, saved by Isandro's quick sleight with the coal scuttle. Emotional beat: the cost of hiding truth in a shrinking room.

chapters.title: The Frozen Crossing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The river freezes hard enough, briefly, to walk. Isandro attempts the crossing with copies for the regional paper and slips through the ice. Emotional beat: desperate hope broken mid-stride.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith pulls Isandro half-dead from the shallows; the copies are lost, but Isandro's memory — and the notebook sewn into a coat lining — survives. Emotional beat: grief for the old invisible self, drowned in the river.

chapters.title: Corven's Offer
chapters.summary: Corven's POV. Corven offers Isandro papers, a legal name, passage out — everything they've never had — in exchange for the notebook and silence. Emotional beat: temptation aimed at the exact wound.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro declines, and understands that a name given by Corven would be another erasure. Corven orders them held until after the armistice, when the files can be burned. Emotional beat: fear answered with selfhood.

chapters.title: The Town Decides
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Hobb, the rescued boy's mother, the ferryman, and Edith's network converge; the whole town becomes witnesses, each signing testimony so no single burning destroys it. Emotional beat: the record made flesh.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Guns
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Corven comes to burn Marlowe House; the town stands in his lantern light, a hundred witnesses with signed pages. He retreats, but the telegraph office is locked against them. Emotional beat: victory that isn't victory yet.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro climbs the telegraph pole in the armistice-eve dark and taps the testimony out by key, signing their own name for the first time — Isandro Galloway, witness. As they finish, the church bells begin: the war is over. Emotional beat: the climax, identity and truth arriving in the same instant.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: Isandro's and Edith's POVs alternating. Spring: Corven arrested as investigators arrive with the published account; the bridge reopens. Isandro, now a named man with a vote to cast, chooses to stay and drive for Edith — by choice, not by hiding. Emotional beat: resolution, memory honored, power answered.
